text: Planting a vegetable garden requires careful planning. Choose a location that receives at least six hours of direct sunlight per day. Test the soil and amend it with compost if necessary to improve drainage and nutrient content. Plan your layout based on the spacing requirements of each plant and consider companion planting to maximize growth and minimize pests. Start seeds indoors about six weeks before the last frost date and transplant them outdoors when the soil temperature is consistently above sixty degrees.

To make a basic sourdough starter, combine equal parts flour and water in a clean glass jar. Stir thoroughly until no dry flour remains. Cover loosely and let it sit at room temperature for twenty-four hours. Each day, discard half of the starter and feed it with fresh flour and water. After about five to seven days, you should notice bubbles forming and a pleasant sour smell. This indicates that the wild yeast has become active and the starter is ready to use.
